isCmsPath

The CMS is a separate document/app (cms/index.html) — /cms and /admin are hard navigations so the CMS boots in isolation. In production the firebase.json rewrites cover this; in dev Vite resolves /cms to the CMS document directly. The clean /cms path keeps index.html out of the address bar — the rewrite stays internal to hosting.

setMetaContent

Writes content into one head selected by selector; no-ops when absent. Exported for views that resolve their title asynchronously (project data lands after navigation) and must keep the social mirrors in step.

setMetaDescription

Pushes a resolved description into every description-bearing head meta — description, og:description, twitter:description, DC.Description and og:image:alt (the share card's alt text mirrors the snippet). Views call this after their localized content node resolves, since route parsing runs before the per-locale data chunks land.

syncDocumentHead

document.title + canonical sync for the resolved route — extended to the social/url mirrors (og:title, twitter:title, DC.Title, og:url, twitter:url) so every head tag agrees with the active route instead of keeping the homepage values the shell booted with. meta.canonical normalizes alias URLs (e.g. /portfolio/brazilian-leather → /portfolio/cicb); meta.description feeds the description metas via setMetaDescription.

buildRouteJsonLd

Base JSON-LD entities for a resolved route — exported so views whose localized descriptions resolve post-navigation (home/about) can re-emit the graph with the real description instead of the parse-time fallback, and so rich views can append entities to the same base. canonicalOverride lets syncDocumentHead pass the URL it already computed for the so both stay identical.

  • @param to Resolved route descriptor.
  • @param canonicalOverride Canonical URL; recomputed from to when absent.
  • @param description Description override (post-fetch localized text).
  • @returns JSON-LD entity array for updateJsonLd().

syncScroll

Anchored routes (#about/#contact) wait 300ms — long enough for the home view's dynamic chunk to mount its shadow DOM — then deepQuerySelector pierces that shadow to find the marker element. All other routes hard-reset to top so the new view doesn't inherit the previous page's scroll depth.
